findings.title: Modbus/TCP exposed on 502/tcp
findings.evidence: nmap: 502/tcp open, service 'modbus Modbus TCP'
fix: Do NOT scan aggressively or patch live controllers: open a Management of Change (MOC) with Process Safety before any intervention.

Contain first: add a deny rule at the IT/OT boundary (conduit) so the protocol is only reachable from the engineering workstations and historian in the OT DMZ (zones and conduits model, IEC 62443 style).
Enable the controller's write-protection / run-mode key or protocol allowlist where the vendor supports it.
Plan the permanent fix (firmware, segmentation redesign) for the next scheduled turnaround and record it in the plant maintenance system.
verify: Passive check: from the corporate IT VLAN, a single TCP connect test (nc -zv <ip> <port>) must fail; no active protocol scanning on production.
OT-ENG confirms with the asset owner that HMI/historian communication is unaffected (sign-off in MOC).
findings.detect: SOC + OT-ENG: passive OT network monitoring rule for any IT-sourced Modbus/S7/DNP3/EtherNet-IP session, and for write/program-download function codes.
findings.category_title: Industrial control protocol reachable from outside the OT zone
routing_notes: Requires Management of Change (MOC) and process-safety sign-off before any change on live equipment.

findings.tester_notes: Manual test with two supplier accounts
fix: Enforce an object-level authorization check on the server for every request that takes an object identifier (owner or tenant match).
Centralise the check in a policy middleware instead of per-controller code.
Use non-sequential identifiers as defence in depth (never as the only control).
Add negative authorization tests (user A cannot read user B) to CI.
verify: Repeat the request with a second low-privilege account; the API must return 403/404.
Automated authorization test suite passes.
findings.detect: SOC: alert on a single session enumerating many object IDs in a short window.
findings.category_title: Broken access control (IDOR / BOLA)
findings.why: P2 because the tester or the scanner confirmed it can be exploited, the asset is reachable from the internet and its business criticality is 4/5 (CVSS v4 7.1).
findings.business_impact: Supplier portal supports 'Procurement and supplier onboarding' (criticality 4/5, production, zone DMZ, internet-facing; data: personal). If exploited, an attacker could read or modify application data and act as other users.

findings.title: OpenSSH 8.9p1: CVE-2024-6387 +1 more
findings.evidence: nmap NSE vulners: cpe:/a:openbsd:openssh:8.9p1: |     	CVE-2024-6387	8.1	https://vulners.com/cve/CVE-2024-6387 |     	CVE-2023-48795	5.9	https://vulners.com/cve/CVE-2023-48795
fix: Confirm the exact installed version and the vendor advisory for every CVE listed.
Apply the vendor fixed release (or the supported LTS branch) through the normal change process; emergency change if the CVE is in CISA KEV.
If patching must wait, apply the vendor workaround or put the service behind an allowlist / WAF virtual patch and document the compensating control with an expiry date.
Add the component to the software inventory (SBOM / CMDB) so the next advisory is matched automatically.
verify: Re-run the version detection scan (nmap -sV --script vulners) and confirm the banner or package reports the fixed version.
Re-run the original exploit check (non-destructive) and confirm it fails.
findings.detect: Alert on exploitation patterns for the listed CVEs at the edge (WAF/IDS) and on unexpected child processes of the service.
findings.category_title: Outdated software with known vulnerabilities

findings.title: VNC exposed on 5900/tcp
findings.evidence: nmap: 5900/tcp open, service 'vnc VNC protocol 3.8'
fix: Remove the direct exposure: close the port on the perimeter firewall / security group for any source outside the admin allowlist.
Publish remote administration only through the corporate VPN or a zero-trust access broker with MFA.
Enforce Network Level Authentication (RDP) or key-only authentication (SSH) and disable password logins for privileged accounts.
Record the rule change with ticket ID in the firewall change log.
verify: From an external vantage point, nmap -Pn -p <port> <public IP> must report filtered/closed.
Confirm the service is still reachable through the VPN / broker path for authorised admins.
findings.detect: SOC: alert on successful logons to this service from non-VPN source ranges and on password-spray patterns.
findings.category_title: Remote administration service reachable from untrusted networks

verify: External request to the admin path returns 403/404.
Admin access works from the admin network with MFA.
findings.detect: SOC: alert on admin path access from external IPs.

findings.title: SNMP exposed on 161/udp (unauthenticated read)
findings.evidence:
nmap: 161/udp open, service 'snmp SNMPv1 server; public' | snmp-info: enterprise: ciscoSystems
  engineIDFormat: unknown
  community: public (read)
fix: Migrate the device to SNMPv3 with authPriv (SHA-2 + AES).
If v2c must stay temporarily, set a long random read-only community and an ACL that allows only the NMS address.
Disable SNMP write access entirely.
verify: nmap -sU -p161 --script snmp-info <host> with 'public' must fail.
NMS still polls the device over SNMPv3.
findings.detect: SOC: alert on SNMP requests from sources other than the NMS.
findings.category_title: SNMP v1/v2c with default or guessable community string

findings.title: Phishing simulation: 18% click rate and 7% credential submission
findings.evidence: Campaign Q3: 412 recipients, 74 clicks, 29 credential submissions, 6 reports to SOC
fix: Run short, role-based awareness sessions for the affected teams within 30 days (no blame, focus on reporting).
Deploy a one-click 'report phishing' button and publish the reporting channel.
Enforce MFA so a captured password alone is not enough.
Schedule a follow-up simulation in 90 days to measure improvement.
verify: Follow-up simulation click rate below the agreed target; report rate above target.
findings.detect: SOC: triage queue for user-reported phishing with SLA.
findings.category_title: Users susceptible to phishing / social engineering

findings.title: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
findings.evidence: ZAP plugin 40012, risk 3: https://suppliers.novarefino.example/onboarding/step2?company= | evidence: <scrIpt>alert(1);</scRipt>
fix: Apply context-aware output encoding in the template layer for the affected parameter (HTML, attribute, JS, URL contexts).
Enable the framework's auto-escaping and remove any raw/unsafe rendering helpers in the affected view.
Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (no unsafe-inline) as defence in depth.
Set HttpOnly on session cookies so injected script cannot read them.
verify: Replay the payload; it must render as inert text.
ZAP passive + active scan shows no XSS alert for the endpoint.
findings.detect: SOC: CSP violation reports forwarded to SIEM; alert on spikes.

findings.title: Port scans and password spraying generated no SOC alert
findings.evidence: Full nmap sweep and 600 spraying attempts over 2 days; no ticket raised by SOC
fix: Onboard the missing log source (host, firewall, application) to the SIEM with parsing validated.
Create or tune the detection for the ATT&CK techniques used during the test, using the ATT&CK v20 detection strategies as a starting point.
Add the scenario to the purple-team regression list.
verify: Replay the test activity (atomic test) and confirm an alert is raised and triaged within the SOC SLA.
findings.detect: This ticket IS the detection work.

findings.title: Missing web security headers / insecure cookie attributes (2 issues)
findings.evidence: ZAP plugin 10038, risk 2: https://suppliers.novarefino.example/; https://suppliers.novarefino.example/onboarding/ || ZAP plugin 10010, risk 1: https://suppliers.novarefino.example/login | evidence: Set-Cookie: SESSIONID || Burp low/firm: /login [SESSIONID cookie]
merged_titles: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set (2 URLs)
fix: Add Strict-Transport-Security (max-age >= 1 year), Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options and frame-ancestors at the reverse proxy for all virtual hosts.
Set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite on session cookies in the framework configuration.
Keep the header set in a shared proxy snippet under version control.
verify: curl -sI https://<host> shows the headers; ZAP passive scan shows no header alerts.
Browser dev tools show the cookie flags.
findings.detect: Track through configuration compliance; no SOC rule needed.
findings.category_title: Missing web security headers / insecure cookie attributes

findings.title: TLS Version 1.0 Protocol Detection
findings.evidence: Nessus plugin 104743: TLSv1.0 is enabled and the server supports at least one cipher.
fix: Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1; keep TLS 1.2 with AEAD ciphers and TLS 1.3.
Scanner guidance: Enable TLS 1.2 or 1.3 only.
Replace self-signed or expiring certificates with certificates from the corporate or public CA and automate renewal.
Apply the change through a shared hardening baseline (Ansible/GPO) so every web front end gets it.
verify: nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p443 <host> must show no TLS 1.0/1.1 and grade A ciphers only.
testssl.sh <host> shows no high or critical items.
findings.detect: Low detection value; track through configuration compliance scanning.
findings.category_title: Weak TLS configuration (old protocol versions or ciphers)

findings.title: FTP exposed on 21/tcp
findings.evidence: nmap: 21/tcp open, service 'ftp vsftpd 3.0.3'
fix: Replace Telnet with SSH and FTP with SFTP/FTPS; disable the cleartext daemon after migration.
Rotate every credential that was ever used over the cleartext protocol.
Block the cleartext port at the host firewall so it cannot be re-enabled silently.
verify: nmap -p 21,23 <host> must report closed/filtered.
Confirm that the replacement encrypted service accepts logins with rotated credentials.
findings.detect: SOC: network sensor rule for any new Telnet/FTP session on the segment.
findings.category_title: Cleartext management or file-transfer protocol in use
